title: When to Play a Provisional Ball
question: You think your ball may be out of bounds but are not certain. What should you do?

choices.text: Wait until you reach the area and decide.
Immediately declare the original ball lost.

explanation: To save time, a player may play a provisional ball under Rule 18.3 if they think their ball may be lost outside a penalty area or out of bounds. This allows the player to avoid a long walk back if the original ball is not found or is out of bounds.

juniorVersion.title: What to Do If You Think Your Ball Might Be Out
juniorVersion.question: You think your ball might be out of bounds, but you are not sure. What should you do before you go look for it?

choices.text: Walk up to where you think your ball is and then decide what to do.
Hit another ball now, just in case, and call it a provisional ball.
Say straight away that your first ball is lost.

juniorVersion.explanation: If you think your ball might be out of bounds, you can hit a provisional ball before walking to look for your first one. This saves time, in case your first ball cannot be found or is out of bounds.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A ball you play just in case your first ball is lost or out of bounds.
A place outside the golf course where you are not allowed to play from.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Act out a situation where a ball might be out of bounds to show when to play a provisional ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they must always look for their ball first.
They might think they cannot play a provisional ball unless an adult tells them.
